projects.description: Most e-commerce chatbots are bad: wrong answers, frustrated customers, more support tickets than they close. Claricart is an AI support tool that actually understands the store: product catalog, order history, return policies, all of it. We distribute via Shopify as a subscription app. Beyond chat, we're building analytics that surface what store owners can't see in Shopify alone: unmet demand, price sensitivity, and gaps between how customers search and how products are described.
projects.role description: Build ML-powered pipelines to extract insights from e-commerce customer conversation logs. Responsibilities include ETL pipeline design, NLP/sentiment analysis on chat transcripts, topic modeling, and creating dashboards for store owners integrated into the ClarityCart app. You'll work with MongoDB, Shopify data, and LLM-based workflows to surface demand signals, product gaps, and customer pain points, overall insights. Preferred: JavaScript, Python, Pandas, OpenAI API, prompt engineering. Familiarity with e-commerce data models and MongoDB is a plus.

We distribute via Shopify as a subscription app. Beyond chat, we're building analytics that surface what store owners can't see in Shopify alone: unmet demand, price sensitivity, and gaps between how customers search and how products are described.
projects.role description: You'll work across the full Claricart stack: a Node.js RAG service that embeds product data into LanceDB for AI-powered chat, a Remix/React store owner dashboard, and an embeddable chat widget. You'd touch the embedding pipeline, vector search, order/cart tooling, the Shopify admin UI, and the widget. Active development right now is an analytics dashboard that surfaces conversation-driven insights (demand signals, price sensitivity, product gaps) using MongoDB and Shopify sales data. Full-stack experience required, RAG experience is a plus.

projects.role description: Claricart's target users are independent Shopify store owners who are skeptical of AI hype and don't respond to generic SaaS marketing. You'll own early growth from zero: figure out which channels reach these people, create content that demonstrates value without overselling, and run outreach that doesn't feel like spam. The goal is our first 10 real paying merchants. If you've built something from nothing before, tell us about it.

projects.description: A technology initiative to automate the detection and elimination of unauthorized live sports streaming. Using web-scraping combined with Al, the system identifies and flags illegal streams — replacing what is currently a slow, manual enforcement process — to protect broadcast rights and revenue for rights holders like the UFC.
projects.role description: Data Engineers / ML Track - Building and maintaining the data infrastructure needed to identify, classify, and track infringing content at scale. Experience with streaming data pipelines preferred.

projects.description: We're building autonomous robots that detect leaks in fluid and gas piping systems, combining physical hardware with cloud-connected sensing software. Current leak detection methods are outdated, slow, and dangerous. We're replacing soapy water that bubbles with a smarter system that works in real time. Both the hardware and software sides are being built from scratch.
projects.role description: The hardest problem right now isn't technical. It's figuring out which customer to go after first. Data centers? Water utilities? Industrial pipelines? Each has different buyers, different purchasing cycles, and different regulatory environments. You'll research the landscape, talk to people in these industries, and help the team make a defensible market entry decision. Expect to build frameworks, throw some of them out, and land on something real through iteration.

Current leak detection methods are outdated, slow, and dangerous. We're replacing soapy water that bubbles with a smarter system that works in real time. Both the hardware and software sides are being built from scratch.
projects.role description: You'll build the cloud-connected software that ties the robot's onboard sensors to a real-time monitoring dashboard. This includes sensor data pipelines, anomaly detection logic, and an interface that lets operators see what's happening inside a pipe without being near it. Python and comfort with embedded systems or IoT is ideal. If you've built anything that collects, processes, and visualizes live sensor data, we want to talk to you.

projects.role description: You'll work on the robot itself: chassis design, locomotion mechanisms, suction-based adhesion for anchoring to pipe walls, and integration of pressure and gas sensors. We're prototyping with access to UCSD fabrication resources. CAD required (SolidWorks or Fusion 360). We want someone who can go from sketch to physical prototype and isn't precious about iterating when something doesn't work, because it will break, and that's the job.

projects.description: Lung cancer is one of the most survivable cancers if caught early. Most cases aren't. We're building a breathalyzer that detects lung cancer biomarkers non-invasively, fast, and affordably, making early screening accessible in clinics that currently can't justify CT programs. Revenue model: devices sold or leased to hospitals, recurring income from single-use sensor cartridges.
projects.role description: Medical devices live or die by their commercial strategy long before FDA approval. You'll map the regulatory pathway we need to navigate, figure out which customer buys first (hospitals, independent clinics, insurance-driven programs, or home health), and build the financial case for each. You'll also run stakeholder interviews with clinicians and hospital administrators to pressure-test our assumptions. No biotech background required. Intellectual curiosity and comfort with ambiguity are non-negotiable.

projects.role description: You'll work on the physical breathalyzer device, integrating biosensors that detect volatile organic compounds in breath, designing the single-use cartridge system, and running benchtop tests to validate sensitivity and specificity. This is real prototype development, not simulation. Biomedical engineering, chemistry, or electrical engineering background is a strong plus. Experience with biosensors, microfluidics, or analytical instrumentation is especially valuable.

projects.role description: A medical device that feels trustworthy in a clinical environment is a completely different design challenge from a consumer product. You'll own the industrial design direction for the breathalyzer: what it looks like, how it feels to use, and how it communicates results to both patients and clinicians. You'll also design our brand identity and presentation materials for investor and hospital pitches. Figma required; some sense of physical product design is a plus.

projects.description: AleraAI is a mobile app that predicts safety risks in real time, guides users toward safer routes, and gives universities and campus security teams actionable data. We're starting with students and commuters and selling the institutional layer to universities and law enforcement. Real predictive intelligence, real B2B revenue model, not just a crime map with a better UI.
projects.role description: Our go-to-market depends on cracking the university partnership model, which means understanding exactly how campus safety offices make purchasing decisions, who the actual budget holders are, and what a compelling pilot proposal looks like to them. You'll research UCSD's existing safety infrastructure, map the decision-making chain, design a pilot program structure, and build the outreach materials to get us in the room. If this goes well, you'll be the person who landed our first institutional customer.

projects.role description: You'll build the core mobile app: real-time location processing, risk scoring logic based on incident and environmental data, and push alert systems. We're targeting React Native or Flutter for cross-platform. You'll also work on the data pipeline feeding the prediction model. Strong comfort with location APIs, real-time data streams, and mobile development required. This is a zero-to-one build. You'll be making architectural decisions that matter, not implementing a spec someone else wrote.

projects.role description: Safety is something people care deeply about but don't love being marketed to about. Your challenge is to build genuine community around AleraAI, starting with UCSD students, without it feeling like a fear campaign. You'll run our social channels, design student-facing content, and develop grassroots activation strategies: tabling, partnerships with student orgs, word-of-mouth loops. Strong writing required. Experience with campus organizing or community building is a big plus.

projects.description: Students apply aimlessly and miss opportunities that actually fit them. We're building an AI platform that matches students to the right opportunities, helps them build stronger applications, and gives universities a tool to license for their entire student body. The market is crowded, which means the only path is finding the gap none of them fill and owning it completely.
projects.role description: You'll answer the most important question facing this project: who is not being served by Handshake, LinkedIn, or any existing tool, and why? That means deep competitive research, user interviews with students and recent grads across different majors and backgrounds, and a clear point of view on our differentiated positioning. You'll also model the university licensing opportunity and structure what a deal with a career center looks like. First-gen students and people from underrepresented backgrounds are especially encouraged to apply. Your experience navigating recruiting is exactly the insight we need.

projects.role description: You'll build the core platform from scratch: the opportunity matching engine, the AI application builder that helps students tailor their materials, and the user dashboard. Full-stack work: backend data pipelines, LLM API integration for the AI features, and a fast front-end. We want it to feel noticeably better than Handshake from the first click. Full-stack experience required; LLM API experience a major plus.

Your job is to make sure they know about this platform before they send their next application blindly into the void. You'll design and run student-to-student growth campaigns, build referral loops, and find the distribution channels that actually move the needle on campus: social, tabling, student org partnerships, and whatever else works. Target: 100 users by end of quarter.

content.value: The Engineering Innovators and Entrepreneurs Club (EIEC) is a student-run organization at UC San Diego that turns engineering talent into entrepreneurial builders. We work with real ventures and give students the experience of building from zero to one.
Turning engineers into innovators and entrepreneurs.

At EIEC, we empower UC San Diego students to build ventures, solve real-world problems, and create what doesn't yet exist. We're shifting the campus focus from purely job-oriented pursuits toward innovation and entrepreneurship.

We foster an environment where students develop entrepreneurial thinking, tackle real challenges, and merge technical skills with business acumen. Our members don't just gain professional skills. They build the mindset and network to imagine, lead, and create.
Work on actual startups from concept to prototype. Real problems, real users, real stakes.
Engineers, designers, and business strategists working together, the way real startups work.
We host workshops, speaker events, and general body meetings throughout the quarter to help you grow.
Join a community of builders. Whether you want to collaborate, learn, or just get inspired, we're here.
The people running EIEC. Students who've been in the trenches and are building the org they wish existed when they started.
Whether you're interested in joining us, partnering, or just want to learn more, reach out.
We're currently recruiting. Check out our open projects and apply.

EIEC's portfolio of early-stage ventures is looking for students to join as volunteer interns. These are zero-to-one projects: scrappy, ambiguous, and genuinely exciting. You won't be shadowing anyone. You'll be doing the work.

Six venture teams working across robotics, biotech, AI, and consumer products.
